html:
Aum Shinrikyo was a Japanese religious movement founded in 1984 by Chizuo Matsumoto, who called himself Shoko Asahara, and is best known for the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack. It began as a small yoga school in Tokyo.

Asahara mixed yoga, Buddhism and Hindu ideas with prophecies of a coming world war. By the early 1990s the group had thousands of members in Japan and many more in Russia. It drew in well-educated people, including doctors and scientists, and asked them to give up property and family. It was recognised as a religious body in 1989, the same year its members killed a lawyer, Tsutsumi Sakamoto, who was helping families fight it, along with his wife and infant son.

After a failed bid for parliament in 1990, the group turned to violence. It built a weapons programme and made sarin, a nerve gas, which it used in Matsumoto in 1994 and in Tokyo in 1995. Police raided its sites, and Asahara was arrested in May 1995.

Asahara and twelve others were executed in 2018. The group was banned from some rights but not dissolved as a faith, and successor groups, including one named Aleph, still exist under watch.
sum: Aum Shinrikyo was a Japanese religious movement founded in 1984 by Chizuo Matsumoto, who called himself Shoko Asahara, and is best known for the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack. It began as a small yoga school in Tokyo.
